newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS--NYMEX crude ends higher on Iraq news.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS--NYMEX crude ends higher on Iraq news.

text.p: NYMEX oil prices ended higher Tuesday after bullish news in the U.S.-Iraqi conflict triggered short covering, and pulled oil prices out of negative territory, said traders.
"News that Iraq was saying that it thinks the U.S. will strike was a little supportive at the end," said a trader.
Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz said the United States was beefing up its military presence in the Middle East Gulf to launch another military strike against Iraq country.
Crude oil for October delivery on the New York Mercantile Exchange settled up 12 cents to $23.31, after rising as high as $23.73 and falling as low as $22.97 during the day.
October heating oil settled up 0.30 cent to 65.59 cents, and October gasoline settled off 0.13 cent to 62.74 cents.
"The market is trying to carve out a range for itself," said Smith Barney analyst John Saucer.

NYMEX crude oil prices have been on a rollercoaster ride after being sent near the post-Gulf War high of $25.70 following military incursions by Saddam Hussein's troops into northern Kurdish regions in Iraq.

Prices fell more than $1.00 Monday following an unsubstantiated report that the United States had asked Saudi Arabia to increase oil ouput. The report was denied by Middle East Gulf sources and U.S. State Department officials.
"Prices came back to cover the territory they lost yesterday on that false report," said Fimat USA Futures analyst Rita Beale.

News that the United States was sending 3,500 Army troops to Kuwait and that two patriot anti-missile batteries had arrived in Suadi Arabia was only bullish enough to temporarily bolster the rebound in crude.
Prices turned south shortly before the close and analysts said the near-term prospects for crude are uncertain.
"The market is going to be choppy, but the fundamentals are in place," said Smith Barney's Saucer.
Meanwhile, the market awaited weekly oil inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) which was expected out Tuesday evening.
Traders were expecting a seasonal build of about 2 million barrels for distillate stocks. Heating oil prices have been strong due to historically low distillate inventories.
For the week ended September 6, the API said heating oil stocks were 19.3 million barrels below a year ago. Total distillate stocks were 17.1 million barrels below a year ago.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
